pages.text: Anum had a flat balloon. “Is there anything in it?” she asked. Uncle Ocloo said, “Blow into it and see.” Anum blew. The balloon grew round and big.
sentences: Anum had a flat balloon.
“Is there anything in it?” she asked.
Uncle Ocloo said, “Blow into it and see.” Anum blew.
The balloon grew round and big.
pages.alt: In a sunny Ghanaian family compound, Anum blows into a bright red balloon until it swells round and big while Uncle Ocloo watches warmly.

pages.text: “What filled the balloon?” asked Uncle Ocloo. “Air,” said Anum. “I cannot see it, but it took up space.” She let go of the end. The balloon whizzed around and went flat again.
sentences: “What filled the balloon?” asked Uncle Ocloo.
“Air,” said Anum.
“I cannot see it, but it took up space.” She let go of the end.
The balloon whizzed around and went flat again.
pages.alt: Anum laughs with delight as the released red balloon zooms through the air in swirls before fluttering down flat beside Uncle Ocloo.

pages.text: Anum made a paper fan. She waved it near her face and felt a soft wind. “Moving air makes wind,” said Uncle Ocloo. “It is all around us, even when we cannot see it.”
sentences: Anum made a paper fan.
She waved it near her face and felt a soft wind.
“Moving air makes wind,” said Uncle Ocloo.
“It is all around us, even when we cannot see it.”
pages.alt: Sitting on a wooden bench on the veranda, Anum waves a folded colourful paper fan near her smiling face as ribbons in her hair lift gently in the breeze.

pages.text: At his shop, Uncle Ocloo pumped air into a bicycle tyre. The tyre grew hard. “Air in a tyre makes the ride smooth,” he said. In the yard, her little brother’s kite lifted up in the wind.
sentences: At his shop, Uncle Ocloo pumped air into a bicycle tyre.
The tyre grew hard.
“Air in a tyre makes the ride smooth,” he said.
In the yard, her little brother’s kite lifted up in the wind.
pages.alt: Outside his small roadside bicycle repair shed, Uncle Ocloo pumps air into a bicycle tyre with a hand pump while Anum’s little brother flies a colourful kite in the yard.

pages.text: “We use air, too,” said Anum. She put her hand on her chest and breathed in and out. “Every person, animal and plant needs air to live,” said Uncle Ocloo. “And wet clothes dry faster in moving air.”
sentences: “We use air, too,” said Anum.
She put her hand on her chest and breathed in and out.
“Every person, animal and plant needs air to live,” said Uncle Ocloo.
“And wet clothes dry faster in moving air.”
pages.alt: Anum stands with her hand on her chest breathing calmly beside Uncle Ocloo, while clean colourful laundry billows on a washing line in the breeze behind them.

pages.text: That evening, Anum drew a bright picture of her invisible helper showing five jobs for air: filling a balloon, making wind, pumping a tyre, lifting a kite and helping us breathe.
sentences: That evening, Anum drew a bright picture of her invisible helper showing five jobs for air: filling a balloon, making wind, pumping a tyre, lifting a kite and helping us breathe.
pages.alt: At a wooden table in warm evening light, Anum uses coloured pencils to draw five wordless little pictures showing a balloon, a paper fan, a bicycle, a kite and a smiling child.

activities.question: What do people, animals and plants need to live?
